title: Passwords in key-value connection strings: quoted, escaped and delimiter-terminated
summary: Key-value connection strings that hold a synthetic password: libpq keyword/value with single quotes, a space and backslash escapes; an ADO.NET string where the password ends at a semicolon; the MySQL key-value form with a quoted string; and a Kafka SASL/PLAIN JAAS line with a double-quoted password ending at a semicolon.
rationale: The secret is bounded by the quoting and delimiter rules of each form, not by whitespace. A libpq value in single quotes may contain spaces, and a single quote or backslash inside it is written \' or \\, so the secret span (source text) includes the backslashes; the decoded value is a different string related by the escaping rule (the escape-decoding link belongs to #94/#95). An ADO.NET password ends at the next semicolon; the JAAS password ends at its closing double quote. Covering only up to the first space, quote or escape leaves the rest of the password in place. The quote characters themselves are delimiters and are not part of the span.

expectation.rationale: Documented grammar fixes where each password sits and where it ends: libpq keyword/value quoting and escapes, the ADO.NET Password keyword inside semicolon-separated pairs, the MySQL key-value form with delimited strings, and the SASL/PLAIN JAAS example password="..." followed by a semicolon. That the project expects these literals to be reported over their full extent is a policy decision, pending a recorded maintainer decision and a non-author reviewer. ADO.NET quoting of values that themselves contain semicolons was not read in the sources fetched and is deliberately not exercised.

sources.supports: In the keyword/value format a value containing spaces is surrounded by single quotes, and single quotes and backslashes within a value must be escaped with a backslash (\' and \\).
A SqlClient connection string places the password in a Password keyword among semicolon-separated keyword=value pairs (User ID=...;Password=...;Initial Catalog=...).

In the key-value form pairs are written { key: value, ... }, strings must be delimited (for example with the single quote), and no percent-encoding is needed; the page shows a password key in this form.
sources.locator: key-value pair section and the password discussion

sources.supports: The SASL/PLAIN client example is sasl.jaas.config=org.apache.kafka.common.security.plain.PlainLoginModule required username="..." password="...";

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Issue #111 (parent #92). Span convention: the characters between the opening and closing quote exclusive of the quotes, escape backslashes included; for the unquoted ADO.NET form, the characters up to but excluding the next semicolon. Related reviews: generic:connection-string-password basis review (#52, owner of evidence-class restoration for the existing family fixtures), sibling grammar and benign cases under the same family in records/cases. Encoded-representation and reconstruction links: #94 and #95 (parent #92).
